name: Dalit feminism
summary: Dalit feminism holds that Dalit women face a distinct oppression produced by caste, gender and class together, and that neither the mainstream (largely upper-caste) women's movement nor a Dalit movement centred on men has addressed it. It draws on Ambedkar's attack on caste and Brahmanical patriarchy, seeks equal rights through law, representation and organisation, and builds standpoint theory from Dalit women's own writing and testimony.
scope: The Indian Dalit feminist tradition as documented by Sharmila Rege (Dalit feminist standpoint, Brahmanical patriarchy), Gopal Guru, Sulochanabai Dongre and the 1942 Nagpur conference, and organisations such as AIDMAM; it takes Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste and Hindu Code Bill as its founding background. Dalit women in Nepal and Pakistan are noted but not the centre. Most statements are outside its subject, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: B. R. Ambedkar
keyFigures.role: Anti-caste thinker and Hindu Code Bill drafter whose writing on caste and women Dalit feminists build on.

sources.usedFor: Summary of Ambedkar's case against caste, the shastras and inter-caste marriage.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Dalit women's greater poverty and exclusion from services is a standing theme, so public provision of care is the natural remedy; the sources do not discuss health policy by name.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Dalit women are concentrated in low-paid, informal labour, and the 1942 Nagpur conference passed resolutions on labour conditions, so higher wage floors fit their agenda.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Dalit women critiqued the New Economic Policy at the Asian and World Social Forums, implying distrust of market-led allocation, though no general doctrine on markets is stated.

public-ownership.rationale: Sources give no stance on nationalisation; Dalit feminists care more about who gets jobs and access than about ownership form, so adherents are not clearly aligned.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concern with Dalit women's poverty and the critique of neoliberal policy suggest support for redistribution, inferred rather than stated.

unions-good.rationale: Dalit women's labour rights were on the agenda from the 1942 conference, and organisation of Dalit women workers is a standard demand, though caste bias inside unions is also criticised.

property-fundamental.rationale: Ambedkar's Hindu Code Bill overrode customary property rules to give women inheritance, so property rights are not treated as untouchable; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The critique of the New Economic Policy suggests support for regulation, inferred from that critique.

cut-welfare.rationale: Dalit women are described as more likely to be poor and marginalised, so cutting welfare would hit them hardest; adherents oppose it.

worker-ownership.rationale: No stated position; collective ownership appeals to a poverty-focused politics but the sources never raise it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Dalit women report that police ignore their complaints and abuse them, so extended state surveillance is distrusted; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources are silent and adherents are not recorded as taking a side.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Caste-based abuse and slurs against Dalit women are part of the violence they document, and the Atrocities Act criminalises caste insults, so legal limits are favoured.

strong-leader.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutional democracy and his insistence on women's equal participation are incompatible with rule by one strong man.

state-harmful.rationale: Dalit feminists press the state to enforce laws and protect Dalit women, so they want a stronger, more accountable state rather than none.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; the issue is far from the Indian Dalit context.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police inaction and abuse toward Dalit women are central complaints, so adherents want accountability rather than more power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Ambedkar opposed prostitution and Dalit feminists describe devadasi and jogini systems as caste-based sexual exploitation of Dalit women, though some stress sex-worker rights; low confidence.

decide-locally.rationale: Village-level caste power is where Dalit women face the worst violence, so devolution to local elites is distrusted in favour of central constitutional protection.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on dignity and non-violence in the Ambedkarite tradition; sources do not address penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Dalit autobiographies expose gender hierarchy inside Dalit families, and the 1942 conference called for divorce rights and an end to polygamy, so patriarchal family structure is not celebrated.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Dalit feminism is inclusive of sexuality questions, but sources do not give a stated position on marriage equality; inferred from equal-rights stance.

abortion-legal.rationale: Sulochanabai Dongre advocated birth control at the 1942 Nagpur conference and Dalit feminists stress women's bodily autonomy; abortion is inferred from that.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ambedkar held religious belief in the shastras to be the root of caste, so a larger public role for (Hindu) religion is resisted.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Remedying caste injustice, including through law and affirmative measures, is the core demand; read as caste for racial injustice, the source describes the movement as seeking equal rights for Dalit women.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Rege and others treat gender roles as produced by caste-patriarchal social relations (Brahmanical patriarchy) rather than nature, though the exact wording is not their own.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Ambedkar demanded the destruction of the shastras and Brahmanical custom, so preserving dominant national tradition is resisted.

gradual-change.rationale: Ambedkar rejected piecemeal reform of caste in favour of destroying its religious basis, and Dalit feminists press for urgent change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not a Dalit feminist issue; no stated position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Dalit women took caste violence to the UN (2018 report) and lobbied at the 2001 World Conference Against Racism, treating international bodies as allies against a stonewalling state.

free-trade.rationale: The critique of the New Economic Policy suggests scepticism toward liberalisation; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Their internationalist UN advocacy suggests scepticism of nation-first politics; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: No documented position; poverty focus cuts against limits on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not a core theme; Dalit communities are among the most exposed to environmental harm, so support is inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Ambedkar favoured constitutional means but also said caste must be destroyed root and branch; adherents split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rege's standpoint approach values the knowledge of marginalised women against credentialled elites, inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Ambedkar favoured democratic constitutionalism and state socialism within it, but sources give no support for full planning; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Wealth redistribution is consistent with their poverty focus; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on Dalit women's poverty and economic dependence.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ambedkar favoured state economic direction for the oppressed; inferred, not stated in the sources opened.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land access for landless Dalit women is a demand, so broad ownership is favoured; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a position held; the movement seeks fair wages for Dalit women rather than abolition of wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No documented position; rejecting market-fundamentalism, inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutionalism and Dalit feminists' reliance on rights and open advocacy are incompatible with one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts Ambedkarite equality; Ambedkar condemned birth-based hierarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Ambedkar's democratic constitutionalism is the tradition they inherit, and women's political participation is measured as the success of a movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: No documented position; reliance on the Indian constitution suggests opposition, inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Ambedkar attacked birth-based hierarchy, and caste is exactly the claim that some are naturally fit to rule or serve; the source rejects it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Ambedkar favoured constitutional methods, but Dalit feminists document violence by caste forces and adherents are not documented as pacifist.

war-builds-character.rationale: No documented position; inferred rejection of militarism.

separate-church-state.rationale: Ambedkar traced caste to religion and the Dalit movement relies on a secular constitution; separating state from Hindu religious authority is favoured.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ambedkar called for destroying belief in the sanctity of the shastras, and burned the Manusmriti; law based on scripture is rejected.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Dalit women rely on public courts and the state to protect them against caste forces; privatised justice would favour local dominant castes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ambedkarite politics is built against birth-based exclusion; a nation defined by ethnicity is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dalit feminists add caste to class and criticise class-only readings, so class struggle is not the main driver; but they do not deny it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They press for equal outcomes through reservation and targeted measures, not only equal opportunity, given the compounded disadvantage of Dalit women.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Dalit and Adivasi struggles are linked in the 'SC/ST' category, but no documented position on land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources note colonial constructions of Dalit women's bodies as sexually available but say nothing on reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: No documented position; inferred rejection of religion-based union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No documented position; collective solidarity is emphasised.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Duty frameworks (dharma) are the language through which caste is enforced; Dalit feminists insist on rights.

limit-population.rationale: Dalit women advocate birth control as choice, not state-imposed limits, so coercive limitation is opposed; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: No documented position; modernity and education are valued as routes out of caste.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No documented position; inferred distrust of unaccountable systems.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste demands destroying the old religious order; the Dalit feminist tradition rejects restoring it.

direct-action.rationale: Dalit women mobilised on the streets and also use legal, UN and electoral routes; both are used.

means-match-ends.rationale: Ambedkar insisted on means as important as ends ('knowing the proper ways and means is more important'); inferred as applied here.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No documented position; plainly outside the movement.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Ambedkar attacked caste as a division of labourers, not the division of labour itself; the statement is not their position.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No documented position; inferred from poverty focus.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Dalit feminists emphasise caste and gender exploitation; profit-as-exploitation is not stated.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Ambedkar rejected dictatorship and class-only revolution; a proletarian dictatorship is not their position.

collective-farming.rationale: No documented position; land to the tiller, inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Redistribution to the poor is wanted; the libertarian claim is rejected.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Dalit feminists press group-specific rights (SC/ST protections, Dalit women's recognition), so rights are not only individual.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Ambedkar and Dalit feminists demand voice and representation; exit offers no remedy within caste society.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is meant to protect rights, not treat citizens as customers; inferred from advocacy demanding state accountability.

positive-liberty.rationale: Ambedkar tied freedom to access to education, work and resources, and Dalit feminists argue formal rights without material means are empty.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rege worked to open academia to Dalit voices, implying it is dominated by upper castes, but the claim that it outranks elected officials is not hers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Caste hierarchy is defended by purity-of-blood arguments, which Ambedkar rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: No documented position; caste bodies are distrusted.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personal loyalty and hierarchy are the grammar of caste; Ambedkar rejected it.

bound-labor.rationale: Devadasi and jogini systems and caste-bound bonded labour are described as forms of coerced Dalit women's labour that the movement opposes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Rege's Dalit feminist standpoint holds that knowledge from Dalit women's experience is situated and that dominant knowledge reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Dalit feminists are split between claims of universal rights and standpoint-specific knowledge.

single-common-good.rationale: Standpoint theory stresses differing interests rather than one common good; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on voice for marginalised workers.

school-vouchers.rationale: Public education access for Dalits is a priority and privatised schooling risks exclusion; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: No documented position; against austerity, inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Ambedkar demanded law and rights, not reliance on the goodwill of rulers (he answered Gandhi's appeals to moral example).

force-without-un.rationale: No documented position; reliance on international bodies, inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Ambedkar urged people to throw off the shastras and follow reason (he embraced Buddhism for its ethics), and Dalit feminists critique scripture.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No documented position; Dalit women in Nepal and Pakistan are also noted as excluded, so inclusive welfare is likelier.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not documented; Dalit women's unpaid and bonded labour makes work conditions unattractive.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The 1942 conference demanded divorce rights and an end to polygamy, and the movement rejects caste-patriarchal gender roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Dalit women face moneylender debt, but a legal ban is not a documented demand.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Caste segregation and untouchability are what Ambedkar and Dalit feminism fight; legal segregation is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Dalit feminists see the state as both caste-biased and a tool for protection, so split.

proportional-representation.rationale: Ambedkar sought political representation of minorities; inferred support for representation by proportion.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rege's Brahmanical patriarchy frames patriarchy as a structural system tied with caste that produces graded violence against women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Complaints that police and officials ignore Dalit women suggest distrust of elites; not a stated generalisation.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits on reproduction contradict their stress on bodily autonomy and Ambedkar's rejection of blood purity.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Complaints of police inaction and abuse are central, and the movement reports to the UN on caste violence, so accountability is demanded.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement demands active state protection, reservations and services; a minimal state would fail Dalit women.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Ambedkar held inter-marriage to be the real remedy for caste, so discouraging mixed marriage is rejected.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equal worth is the Ambedkarite premise against caste; the movement seeks equal rights for Dalit women across caste and gender.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Ambedkar's Hindu Code Bill pursued uniform gender-equal law, but some Dalit feminists worry about minority communities; adherents split, leaning yes.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ambedkar led conversion to Buddhism in 1956 as emancipation, and Dalit women face forced conversion in Pakistan but oppose restriction of free choice.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cow-protection laws are used to target Dalits and Muslims whose livelihoods involve hides and meat; opposition is inferred from caste labour politics.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Hindu scriptural authority and for a secular public sphere.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutionalism rests on popular consent and Dalit women's equal participation.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal contradicts equal rights; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Hindu-nationalist parties are criticised but no position on legal bans is recorded.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Freedom from the arbitrary power of caste and patriarchal superiors fits Rege's analysis; non-domination is not their vocabulary.

separated-powers.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutional design and Dalit feminists' use of courts imply support.

vanguard-party.rationale: Ambedkar rejected Marxist vanguardism; Dalit feminist autonomy suggests the same.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Dalit women are the poorest and most marginalised, so their agenda prioritises the poor.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The movement supports labour organisation by Dalit women.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They attribute Dalit women's poverty to caste and social institutions, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ambedkar sought a society of liberty, equality and fraternity across castes; diversity is not a problem.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Dalit women are most vulnerable when protections are suspended.

party-controls-media.rationale: Dalit voices rely on independent media and publishing to be heard (Dalit literature).

clerical-rule.rationale: Priestly rule is the Brahmin order that Ambedkar and Dalit feminists oppose.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Dalit women's autobiographies and writing exposing caste and sexual violence have been resisted as immoral, so moral censorship is opposed.

recall-officials.rationale: Accountability of officials is demanded; recall itself not documented.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Village caste society is where Dalit women face routine sexual and caste violence (devadasi and jogini systems, ignored complaints), so rural life is not idealised.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Ambedkar and Dalit feminists see education as the means of emancipation.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They reject caste hierarchy within cultures and so do not treat all cultural practices as equal; but reject civilisational ranking.

death-penalty.rationale: No documented position; Dalit feminists have called for harsher punishment after caste rapes, so adherents split; weak lean against.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sulochanabai Dongre pushed family planning in 1942, and gender equality in schooling is a core demand.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Ambedkar urged reason over scripture in education; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from support for the Dalit literature written in regional languages.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents split between minority protection and critique of patriarchal religious law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from rejection of conformity to caste custom.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from critique of neoliberal policy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: They argue formal independence did not change caste and class hierarchy for Dalit women, and critique the New Economic Policy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Ambedkar chaired the constitution drafting; the Constitution is the basis of their rights claims.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Dalit women rely on freedoms to organise; restrictions would hit them.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ambedkar's Hindu Code Bill and Dalit land demands treat property rights as subordinate to equality.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Adherents are likely to support curbing Brahmanical temple privilege but sources are silent.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent claims are the logic of birth hierarchy that Ambedkar's text attacks.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement attributes Dalit women's condition to social structure, and Ambedkar rejected blood-based explanations of caste.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Ambedkar's constitutionalism rejects rulers above law.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No documented position; democracy rather than rule of the few, inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Not documented; the movement honours Ambedkar but its emphasis on women's participation as equals is against personality cults, inferred.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land to the landless Dalits, including women's land rights, is a long-standing demand; sources opened mention poverty and the Hindu Code's property provisions only indirectly.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Ambedkar led mass conversion out of Hinduism in 1956; punishing leaving a religion is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Ambedkar urged Dalit women to reject dress codes marking their inferiority, and the movement insists on women's autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Ambedkar's strategy was equal rights inside India rather than separate homeland; adherents fight for rights in place.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Ambedkar held that beliefs and religion drive caste, against economic determinism.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Ambedkar's constitution and Dalit rights depend on courts protecting minorities against majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: They press for women's representation, and typically for within-quota representation of Dalit women.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolishing birth-based privilege is exactly the Annihilation of Caste programme.

history-own-civilization.rationale: No documented position; rewriting history from below is favoured instead.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial constructions of Dalit women are criticised; tutelage is rejected.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Reservation and targeted measures for Dalits and Dalit women are core demands, read by analogy to caste preferences.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Discrimination in hiring, housing and service by caste is what the movement and Atrocities-law advocacy oppose.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Ambedkar chaired the Constitution drafting committee and Dalit feminists rely on entrenched constitutional rights against local majorities; the sources do not use this phrasing.

elective-rulers.rationale: Ambedkarite democracy rejects hereditary rule in favour of elected representatives.

minority-veto.rationale: A single-member veto would let dominant-caste members block reform; no stated position.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from constitutionalism; not discussed in the sources.

animal-use-humane.rationale: No documented position; meat and hide work are Dalit livelihoods, so adherents resist moralising restrictions.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity from the privileged is the kind of benevolence from above that Ambedkar and Dalit feminists replace with rights.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ambedkar urged Dalit women to join the movement as equals and held women's participation to be the measure of its success.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Rege's analysis of how Brahmanical patriarchy is reproduced through culture and ritual points that way, inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: No documented position beyond critique of neoliberal policy.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Hindu nationalist politics; not stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No documented position; outside their subject.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: No documented position; Ambedkar statues are central, but no stance on contested monuments elsewhere.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Dalit feminism stresses women's specific disadvantages and criticises movements focused on men, so equal attention framing is resisted.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Dalit feminists document intra-community violence against Dalit women as routine; symmetry is not their frame.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Ambedkar rejected 'civilisational' arguments used to defend caste; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Dalit women's unpaid and underpaid domestic and care labour is a recurring concern.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examinations are the traditional route for Dalit entry to state posts but caste bias in them is also criticised; split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The 1942 Nagpur conference called for women's right to divorce, and Ambedkar's bill sought divorce rights.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from concern for the poor; informal workers lack savings.

single-official-language.rationale: No documented position; English and regional languages are used in Dalit writing.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: They treat caste-unequal outcomes as evidence of structural discrimination regardless of intent.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Dalit organisations rely on UN and international support and foreign-funding restrictions are used against NGOs reporting caste violence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from support for birth control and bodily autonomy.

residents-only-property.rationale: No documented position; inferred from anti-exclusion stance.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from concern for Dalit women's poverty.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ambedkar urged people to disobey the shastras, but upheld constitutional law; no general position.

non-intervention.rationale: They appeal to international bodies over caste violence, which cuts against strict non-intervention.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Dalit women are themselves targeted by conspiracy-style stigma; adherents reject it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Ambedkar reformed marriage law to protect women's rights, which presupposes legal marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Complaints that authorities ignore Dalit women's reports suggest support for transparency; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Dalit women's organisations were formal bodies and alliances such as AIDMAM and FEDO.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Dalit women invoked UN bodies against domestic stonewalling, so they do not hold national law above international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Ambedkar's conversion and constitutionalism reject defining India by Hindu religion, and Dalit feminists critique Hindu nation politics (Rege).

defeat-communism.rationale: Ambedkar criticised communism but the sources do not give a position on defeating it.

religion-illusion.rationale: Ambedkar condemned scriptural religion as the root of caste yet embraced Buddhism, so religion is not seen as mere illusion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The critique of the New Economic Policy and the emphasis on Dalit women's poverty imply economic change is needed, though caste change is the main emphasis.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; paid care-work recognition is closer to their concerns.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ambedkar criticised the village as a site of caste oppression, so retreating to small communities is distrusted.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Ambedkar is described as rejecting both caste-blind Marxism and caste-bound tradition, so a third course is a plausible inference; the opened sources do not state it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Dalit feminism contests constructions of Dalit sexuality as deviant and stands for equal rights; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Dalit women need free organising and reporting.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Ambedkar called for destroying belief in the shastras, so blasphemy punishment is anathema.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from criticism of colonial treatment of Dalit women.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Women's participation as equals and Dalit women's own organisation is central.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality of caste and gender is described as the root of Dalit feminism, and caste, gender and class are treated as interconnected systems.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from inclusion of sexuality questions and equal rights; not explicitly documented.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Dalit feminists stand with religious minority women (documented in Pakistan) and reject such claims.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Scripture and divine claims underpin caste, and Ambedkar rejected their authority.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Dalit women report complaints being ignored and silenced, so measures keeping harassment complaints out of court are opposed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from preference for market combined with protection.

rich-first.rationale: Trickle-down reasoning is contradicted by their critique of the New Economic Policy.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The critique of neoliberal policy suggests agreement; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Ambedkar fought for universal franchise for the depressed classes; restricting the vote by property is rejected.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from complaints that Dalit voices are excluded from mainstream media.

racial-franchise.rationale: Ambedkar demanded equal political rights for all castes; group-restricted franchise is the opposite.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from complaints about unresponsive authorities.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Ambedkar held intermarriage as the real remedy to caste, and equal-rights marriage law was his project.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Dalit women also face religious persecution in some contexts and reject boycotts.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Ambedkar held that reinterpretation was not enough and the shastras must be rejected, while others reread tradition; adherents split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Ambedkar embraced Buddhism and did not hold atheism promotion; adherents oppose state imposition.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Dalit women demand police accountability and action, not abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ambedkar sought reserved representation and safeguards for minorities, which is similar in spirit.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Dalit feminism demands equal standing for women in every sphere of authority; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The 1942 conference demanded divorce rights and an end to polygamy, and they reject patriarchal marital authority.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from demand for acknowledgement of caste atrocities.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Ambedkar embraced Buddhism, but he did not hold strict pacifism; adherents split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Continuity with ancient tradition would include Brahmanical order, which they reject.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Rege's critique argued that 'Dalit women' is not a homogenous category and critiqued the notion of difference as identity politics; the movement criticises mainstream feminism for treating all women as having the same problems (Swaroopa Rani).

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Ambedkar's politics rested on rights and institutions, though Buddhism gave it an ethical dimension.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from critique of patriarchal religion.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Ambedkar judged the Manusmriti by its treatment of women and Dalit feminists do likewise; Rege centres his writing on Brahmanical patriarchy.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Dalit women are themselves a minority and subordinated; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Local assemblies would be dominated by caste elites.

family-wage.rationale: The male-breadwinner model assumes a dependent wife, whereas Dalit women have always done paid work and the movement seeks equal pay.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from complaints of reprisal against Dalit women speaking out.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Ambedkar embraced Buddhism for ethics but secular rights frame politics; adherents split.

dense-cities.rationale: No documented position; cities have provided relative anonymity from village caste.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Dalit identity politics asserts distinct group interests of Dalit women, by analogy to racial groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Dalit assertion movements embrace pride in Dalit identity, analogously.

communal-electorates.rationale: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for the depressed classes (Poona Pact context) but sources opened do not discuss this; adherents split.

free-public-college.rationale: Education as the route out of oppression is central to Ambedkarite thought.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Rege criticised authenticity claims based on identity, so essentialist claims about women's values are resisted.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour conditions resolutions at the 1942 conference imply support for organised bargaining.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from critique of the New Economic Policy.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Ambedkar worked through the constitutional state.

sacred-nation.rationale: Sacralised nation echoes Hindu nationalism, which Dalit feminists critique.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Ambedkar's equal-worth premise assumes common humanity.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from concern for Dalit voices in media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Ambedkar judged religions by their social ethics and rejected Hinduism's caste teaching, so he did not treat all as one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from poverty concern for Dalit agricultural labourers.

workers-own-party.rationale: Ambedkar founded a labour party in the 1930s but sources opened do not discuss it.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from bodily autonomy stance; not documented in India context.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Ambedkar's Hindu Code Bill gave daughters a share equal to sons, and the movement demands women's land and property rights.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary caste councils (khap or panchayat) are a source of violence against Dalit women; an official role for customary authorities is opposed.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Dalit women are concentrated in low-paid, informal labour where collective organisation matters, but the sources do not discuss compulsory union rules; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: Dalit feminists stress barriers that exclude poor and marginalised women from political participation; inferred that strict ID rules would be opposed, though not discussed in the sources.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Ambedkar and Dalit feminists reject the authority of the shastras and Brahmanical Hinduism over others; inferred that no single interpretation should have legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Ambedkar held that political democracy needs social democracy; inferred that Dalit feminists would not count a state democratic by elections alone while caste hierarchy persists.

premarital-sex.rationale: Dalit feminism attacks Brahmanical control of women's sexuality and defends women's autonomy; inferred, though the sources do not discuss premarital sex directly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The movement relies on testimony, organisation and UN advocacy by marginalised women, so cutting communications would be opposed; inferred, as the sources predate the issue.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Dalit feminists press for rights, quotas and representation rather than replacing welfare with a cash payment; inferred, the sources do not discuss it.

women-suffrage.rationale: Ambedkar and the 1942 Nagpur conference of Dalit women pressed for women's equal civil and political rights, and the Hindu Code Bill sought equality for women.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Dalit feminists, following Ambedkar, trace women's subordination to Brahmanical patriarchy, which rests on the shastras, so religion is a major cause; they target Hindu orthodoxy rather than all religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Dalit activists link caste discrimination to racial discrimination at the UN, which treats both as socially produced hierarchy; inferred, not stated as a view on race categories.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Dalit feminists seek state action and UN advocacy for women's rights; inferred that dedicated agencies would be supported, though the sources do not name them.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Ambedkar tied Dalit dispossession to caste control of land and favoured state-led redistribution over first-come claims; the sources do not discuss homesteading.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its human-rights framing, including lobbying at the UN; the sources do not discuss criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste says caste can end only by destroying belief in the sanctity of the shastras, and Dalit feminists extend this to the Manusmriti's rules on women.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from its insistence that women's representation and gender equality be built in from the start; the statement's Indigenous and national-group setting is outside its subject.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Ambedkar favoured state socialism in some writings but the question of a bureaucratic state is not discussed.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: Ambedkar championed universal adult franchise and direct representation, and the movement presses for Dalit women's direct representation.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: it opposes the Brahmanical religious order, so a privileged legal status for a traditional religion would run against it.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Dalits are dispersed minorities rather than regional majorities, and Ambedkar sought safeguards such as reserved seats instead of territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred neutral.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Ambedkar's constitutional-order approach favours settled state arrangements; the sources do not discuss borders.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the focus is caste oppression and equal rights, not lifestyle.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed; Dalit women are not an Indigenous majority in a region and adherents are not documented on this.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from its gender-equality demands and Ambedkar's support for women's equal rights; the sources do not discuss conscription.

missingStatements.text: Caste discrimination should be treated as a distinct legal ground of discrimination, alongside race and sex.
missingStatements.rationale: Dalit feminists press for caste to be recognised as a legal ground; a clause protecting Dalit women from caste discrimination was dropped at the 2001 World Conference Against Racism and they continue to lobby the UN.
missingStatements.declined: Caste-specific legal-ground claim; too narrow to be asked of every ideology, and equal-treatment questions are partly covered by correct-racial-injustice.

missingStatements.text: Legal quotas should reserve a share of public jobs, education places and elected seats for historically oppressed groups.
missingStatements.rationale: Ambedkar's tradition rests on representation and targeted measures for Scheduled Castes, and Dalit women's groups press that women within these groups be included; the opened sources describe this only indirectly.

missingStatements.text: Caste hierarchy is sustained by religious texts, and belief in their sanctity must be destroyed to end it.
missingStatements.rationale: Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste states the real remedy is to destroy belief in the shastras, and Dalit feminists extend this to the Manusmriti's treatment of women.

notes: Adherents differ on whether 'Dalit patriarchy' is a valid category (Guru, mainstream feminists) or a misreading of Brahmanical patriarchy (Arya, Rege), on universalist versus standpoint claims, and on the uniform civil code. Many answers on economics and foreign policy are inferred and low-confidence. The Rege essay itself and the full text of Annihilation of Caste were not opened; extracts and summaries were.
